newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BANK OF ENGLAND WARNS CITY FIRMS OVER BONUSES

The Bank of England is getting set to warn the City that big bonuses may tempt bankers into taking reckless and excessive risks with their banks' capital. The report will warn City institutions that there are risks involved when young and inexperienced traders are offered the prospect of huge financial rewards which could blind them to other issues.
-- DISABLED BILL MAY HALT HALIFAX FLOAT FOR A YEAR

The Halifax Building Society is threatening to put back its 12 billion pounds stg flotation by at least a year if the Building Societies (Distribution) Bill currently before parliament is made retrospective. The delay would mean holding back bonus payments for 8.5 million people. The bill suggests that converting societies should pay bonuses to disabled and elderly savers with accounts in trust and not just to the first named account members.
-- WPP CHIEF ON TARGET FOR 3 MILLION POUNDS BONUS

Chief executive of WPP, Martin Sorrell is set to receive the second tranche of his multi-million pound incentive package. The City was reacting to the news that WPP, which is one of the world's largest marketing services groups, had no imminent plans for a share buy-back after revealing a 35 per cent rise in 1996 pre-tax profits to 153.3 million pounds stg. If WPP shares remain above 230p until March 18, Mr Sorrell will receive 1.2 million shares, worth 3 million pounds stg at yesterday's closing price of 252p.
THE TIMES
-- EVERSHOLT FOUR GAINS OVER 40 MILLION POUNDS FROM SALE

A new 'fat cat' row was sparked yesterday over the break up of British Rail, when four directors of the Eversholt train leasing company made 42 million pounds stg profit from the sale of the company. Eversholt was acquired by Forward Trust, a subsidiary of Midland Bank for 726.5 million pounds stg. The biggest single beneficiary of the sale is Andrew Jukes, Eversholt's managing director who will realise around 15.9 million pounds stg from the 110,000 pounds stg he invested in the original management buyout in December 1995. The sale has prompted demands from Labour for a Commons inquiry into the cheap sale of state assets during rail privatisation.
-- MONEY GROWS FASTER AT SAINSBURY'S BANK

The supermarkets group, J Sainsbury, yesterday launched its bank with an instant access account offering customers interest of 5.75 per cent gross on any sum from 1 pound stg, the best interest rates in the market. Account holders will also get a Link cashcard and free phone banking. The bank, which is 55 per cent owned by the supermarket group and 45 per cent by Bank of Scotland, opened for business at 244 Sainsbury's branches in the North of England, the Midlands and Scotland, with nationwide coverage being introduced over the coming months.
-- SALES SPREE HELPS RETAIL SPENDING TO REBOUND

Following a quiet December, high street spending rebounded in January as consumers splashed out in the sales. An increase of 0.6 per cent was recorded taking the annual growth rate to 4.6 per cent. The sharp increase was above market expectations and economists believe the result will ensure that the Bank of England will continue to put pressure on the Chancellor for a base rate rise.
THE GUARDIAN
-- PROFITS BOOST WOOLWICH AS FLOTATION NEARS

In the run-up to its July stock market flotation, the Woolwich Building Society has reported headline profits up by 18 per cent on the back of the booming housing market in the South-east. Its overall market share has risen to 6 per cent, with strong demand for mortgages in its predominantly southern heartland.
-- AIRTOURS HAILS STRONG POUND AS HOLIDAYS ABROAD TAKE OFF

Airtours, the second largest package holiday provider in Britain, yesterday applauded sterling's recent rise in value, claiming that bookings for its holidays this summer were up 45 per cent on the same time last year. The company said that it has not suffered from sterling's rise because it has fixed the prices in areas that are usually hit by exchange rate fluctuations such as jet fuel.
-- COST-CUTTING ANGLIAN TO AXE 300 WATER JOBS

Anglian Water yesterday announced its plans to cut 300 jobs, or 6 per cent of its workforce, in a move to save 10 million pounds stg a year. The jobs to go will be among manual workers employed at its water and sewerage plants and in the division responsible for its pipeline network. The controversial move follows the loss of 900 white collar jobs 18 months ago. The group is to make a 20 million pounds stg provision in its 1996-97 accounts to cover the cost of redundancy and restructuring its business.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- YORKSHIRE WATER LOSES FIRST ROUND OF BILLS BATTLE

Yorkshire Water has been defeated in the first round of a bitter legal battle over increases in bills to Illingworth Morris, one of its largest industrial customers. One of Europe's largest producers of wool fibres, Illingworth Morris has been given the go-ahead by a High Court judge to pursue a legal case against Yorkshire Water, alleging it had been unfairly overcharged. Yorkshire Water will be prevented from recovering 1.5 million pounds stg in unpaid bills until a full hearing, which should take place later this year.
-- FIRSTBUS IN 54 MILLION POUNDS TAKEOVER OF LONDON BUS GROUP

CentreWest, a London and Home counties bus group agreed a 54 million pounds stg takeover deal with FirstBus, the expanding bus and railways group, yesterday. Around 2,000 employees of CentreWest will share in a 7 million pounds stg windfall following the take over, and four directors will net around 9.7 million pounds stg.
-- FRANCE TO AUCTION STAKE IN THOMSON

The French Government intends to seek bids for its 1.3 billion pounds stg controlling interest in Thomson CSF, the defence arm of Thomson SA, the electronics giant. The move follows the government's failed attempt to privatise the entire group in December and its rejection of pleas from the company's senior management for a stock market flotation.
